newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet,no sales-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet,no sales-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet near midday Wednesday, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Bids ranged from $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt but were passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $69.00, with a few at $70.00, sources said.

Last week's sales at $68.00 were expected to be repeated once packers seriously step in to buy. However, some feedlot managers expressed concern that prices could weaken following the recent steep decline in beef values.
Choice heavier-weight beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $1.31 per cwt at $104.66. That price reflected a $3.13 drop in the past week, USDA statistics showed.
However, pressure from the lower beef values could be offset by ideas the lower prices are attracting strong retail buying interest, cattle feeders said.
Beef sales Tuesday was reported by USDA at 367 loads but overall prices were down $1.31 to $2.21 from Monday's.
Fed cattle prices also could be underpinned by talk that packers were short on live supplies and need to buy cattle by Wednesday or Thursday, they said.
